Subject: Operator access & KMS approach — summary and proposed contractual language

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick summary and the contractual position we can commit to in the DPA: 

1) Operator access model (breakglass)
- By default, operator accounts remain disabled for customers in private deployments.
- Retrieval of customer-produced data (including customer-uploaded content and model KV dumps) is only permitted under a documented emergency process requiring:
  a) Two independent approvals — at least one from FinPay (customer approver) and one from Redwood Security (internal approver).
  b) Accesser attestation and purpose statement logged prior to activation.
  c) All activity is recorded to an immutable audit log (WORM) retained for 2 years and made available for customer audit on request.
- We will include a contract clause: "Operator access to customer data shall be restricted to emergency use only, subject to two-party approval and full audit logging; any access must be narrowly scoped and time limited."

2) KMS options
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended for FinPay): Redwood supports customer-provided keys hosted in major cloud HSMs (e.g., AWS CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM). In this model:
  - Key material is generated and retained in customer's HSM. Redwood receives only wrapped keys or performs envelope encryption where the unwrapped key is never exported from the HSM.
  - We will include a binding clause that Redwood personnel cannot access or export key material and will only invoke cryptographic operations requested by the customer's provisioning and runtime APIs.
- If customer cannot host keys, we offer a Redwood-managed KMS with strict role separation and audit controls; we can enumerate the difference in the DPA.

3) Subprocessors and evidence
- Attached is an up-to-date subprocessor registry (the CSV) and our SOC 2 Type II report summary. We commit to providing SOC 2 report under NDA if needed and to notify you 30 days in advance for new subprocessors.

Next steps:
- We'll incorporate the operator access clause and KMS language into a revised DPA and circulate a redline by Monday 26 Jul.
- We can provide a short operator-access runbook and screenshots of audit log exports for your security review.

Attachments: Operator_Access_Proposal_2027-07-22.docx; Subprocessors_Redwood_2027-07-19.csv

Regards,

Following Vivek's note, we've redlined the DPA to include the two-approver breakglass requirement, the KMS customer-managed language, and the subprocessor notification cadence. Attached: updated DPA (PDF) and the substantiating subprocessor CSV.

Summary of agreed points for inclusion in the DPA:
- Data residency: production workloads will be deployed to eu-west-1 for FinPay unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- KMS: default path is customer-managed HSM (CloudHSM/Azure HSM). Redwood will not have access to unwrapped key material.
- Operator access: disabled by default; emergency access requires two approvers (one FinPay, one Redwood) + immutable audit logs; limited scope and retention for any data accessed.
- Subprocessors: current list attached; SOC2 Type II available under NDA; 30-day notification for new subprocessors.

Next steps:
